clue.text: Soon lore will be translated into English

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put into the abbreviation, splitting it open
translating the word lore turns it into something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that some folklore is about to appear in an English version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be translated' makes RELO, and 'into' splits the abbreviation for English around it. 'Soon' is the definition, though it looks like scene-setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere long is an archaic phrase meaning before much time passes, that is, shortly.

clue.text: Books, say, about new times

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes round the letter for new, enclosing it

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
ages are long periods, eras or times

explanation.surface: A librarian noting that books, for instance, cover new periods of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EG around N, giving ENG. 'Books' is a verb here, as in booking a band.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a performer or a room is to engage or reserve it, so books and engages are synonyms.

clue.text: South American figure turned up at four after end of debate

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after that final letter in the answer
the last letter of the word debate is taken
in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sporting or political figure from South America arriving at four o'clock after a debate finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads the pair upwards in this down entry, and 'end of' and 'after' place the E first. Eva Perón, Argentina's first lady, was known as Evita.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita was the popular name of Eva Perón, the celebrated Argentine first lady, a famous South American.

clue.text: Agreed: US city's mostly in American state

parts.note: OK expresses agreement
LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a US city mostly lies within one American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' means at HOME, and 'mostly' drops its last letter to leave HOM. 'American' looks like part of the definition but supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: No good getting upset over church in central Italy initially providing Italian cuisine

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, that is above, the rest
being upset means being knocked over, disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
the church abbreviation goes inside the pair of initial letters
the first letters of central and Italy are taken

explanation.surface: Things going wrong at a church in central Italy, while someone provides Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' rearranges to GNO, 'initially' gives C and I, and 'in' puts the church between them. 'over' places the first part above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made from potato or semolina, a staple of Italian cooking.

clue.text: Concern about sailor: source of trouble in nightclub

indicators.note: the word for concern goes round the sailor

parts.note: care and concern are synonyms, as worry or attention
AB is an able seaman, an ordinary sailor

indicators.note: the source, or start, of the word trouble is its first letter

explanation.surface: A worry that a sailor caused trouble in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the sailor, and 'source of' supplies a final T. AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a venue offering drinks and live entertainment at night, a type of nightclub.

clue.text: Free ticket offered by a US city theater group

parts.note: a comp is a complimentary, that is free, ticket
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A New York theatre troupe handing out a complimentary ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling 'theater' hints at a US theatrical company.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a troupe of actors or dancers who perform together, as in a theatre company.

clue.text: Support? It's got when expressing annoyance

definitions.meaning: a reserve or extra help that supports something
the phrase to get one's ... means to become annoyed

explanation.surface: A query about support, then a riddle about what one gets when irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: when you are annoyed your back is up, as in getting one's back up.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup is reserve help or a fallback, and having your back up means being annoyed.

clue.text: Excessive speechifying has characters switching places — indication of riot?

indicators.note: two of the letters in the word trade positions with each other, giving a new word

parts.note: wordiness is using far too many words

explanation.surface: A long-winded speech whose characters swap places, a sign of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has characters switching places' swaps the W and R of WORDINESS; the clue does not say which pair, but only one swap makes a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiness, noisy disorderly behaviour, is what a riot shows, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Increased current cost of Glastonbury venue?

parts.note: Glastonbury Tor is a famous hill in Somerset
rent is the cost of hiring something

explanation.surface: A question about higher charges at the Glastonbury festival site.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury Tor is a hill in the English county of Somerset; the hire cost of a Tor would be its rent. 'Increased current' looks like rising prices but means a strong flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, powerful flow of water, a current swollen beyond normal strength.

clue.text: Possibly fell over after question in restaurant area

indicators.note: the reversed word follows the question in the answer

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them hard

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read backwards

parts.note: a fell is upland moor in northern England, so a moor is possibly a fell

explanation.surface: Someone may have fallen over after being questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses MOOR to ROOM. A fell is a hill or moor in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillroom is a restaurant, or a part of one, serving grilled food.

clue.text: Appear frightened to have debt while in credit

indicators.note: the debt word is placed inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: to owe is to have a debt

explanation.surface: Someone frightened at being in debt even while their account looks in credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or shrink back in fear, visibly showing fright.

clue.text: Very clear this writer taps into a lot of elegance

indicators.note: the setter's name is placed inside the shortened word, as a tap into a pipe
most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: grace is elegance of movement or manner
Phi is the setter of this puzzle

explanation.surface: A writer drawing on a store of elegance to be very lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter, Phi, not the usual I or ME. 'a lot of' trims the final letter and 'taps into' puts the name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic means vividly explicit, described in clear and striking detail.

clue.text: Abandon barring women boarding vehicle? On the contrary, becoming insulting

indicators.note: boarding means going inside, as passengers board
the opposite of what is said happens, so the vehicle goes into the shortened word
barring means excluding, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to waive a right is to abandon it
a bus is one kind of vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a ban on women getting on a bus, and things turn insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barring' removes the women letter to leave AIVE. 'On the contrary' flips 'boarding': the vehicle takes in those letters instead of entering it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive language is rude and offensive, the same as insulting.

clue.text: Novel not with Smiley is serious stuff

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spy novel lacking George Smiley would be grim reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' rearranges the letters of NOT and SMILEY. George Smiley is John le Carré's spymaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemnity is seriousness of manner or occasion, a grave quality.

clue.text: Programmes to include tune arranged for string players

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: lists of items, as running orders, are programmes

indicators.note: arranged music is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Concert programmes including a tune arranged for a string section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives UTEN and 'to include' puts it after the first letter of the programmes word. 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutenists play the lute, a plucked stringed instrument, so they are string players.

clue.text: Sailor accounting for most of ship's weight

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: tare is the unladen weight of a vehicle or container

explanation.surface: One sailor said to make up most of a ship's weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of TARE. TAR is a crossword name for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar, or just tar, is an old slang name for a seaman.

clue.text: Opening race not without content

indicators.note: the insides of both words are emptied, leaving only their outer letters

explanation.surface: The race to open something was not without substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without content' empties RACE and NOT to RE and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or split in cloth, an opening torn in it.

clue.text: US state about to encourage fairground attraction

indicators.note: the state abbreviation goes round the other word

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California
to rouse people is to stir or encourage them

explanation.surface: A US state about to promote a funfair ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' but is the containment signal, and California takes its three-letter short form here.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, a classic ride at a fair.

clue.text: Jazz fans getting half of performers rejected

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is affected
rejected means sent back, so that stretch is reversed

parts.note: acts are performers on a bill

explanation.surface: Jazz enthusiasts turning away half the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' and 'rejected' reverse only the first half of ACTS: AC becomes CA, and TS stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is old jazz-age slang for enthusiasts or musicians, hip people who love the music.

clue.text: Legendary castle attended by fate

parts.note: to attend is to come along
your lot is your fate in life

explanation.surface: A legendary castle visited, with fate looming.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the castle and court of King Arthur in British legend.

clue.text: Meat dish I scarf rudely — look

indicators.note: done rudely, in a rough fashion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to see is to look

explanation.surface: A diner admits to gobbling a meat dish rudely, and calls attention to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' rearranges I SCARF to FRICAS. Scarf is US slang for eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a stew of sliced meat, often chicken, in a white sauce.

clue.text: Goes overseas often to take in a lot of historic and curious buildings

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the other letters inside it

parts.note: travellers going abroad usually fly

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: old means historic

explanation.surface: A frequent traveller abroad who visits many historic and odd buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops a final letter and 'to take in' puts the result after the F. A folly is a whimsical ornamental building on a British country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Follies are eccentric decorative buildings with no practical purpose, built for show.

clue.text: Consumes specifically targeted jokes on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word's sound is meant

parts.note: in-jests would be in-jokes, jokes aimed at a particular group

explanation.surface: Someone takes in jokes aimed at them on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: IN-JESTS, like in-jokes, is a stretch on its own, but the pair sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, to consume it.

clue.text: Economic skill picked up? Just the opposite

parts.note: ECON is an abbreviation for economics or economic

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Does economic skill get noticed? No, quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like a homophone signal but here reverses ART to TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: E contra is a Latin phrase meaning on the contrary, the converse.

clue.text: Calm when covered by gross oily stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue the gross abbreviation sits on top, covering the calm word below it

parts.note: GR is an abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen
ease is calm, freedom from worry

explanation.surface: Calm when smeared in thick grease.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'when covered by' puts GR above EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is thick oily matter, used as lubricant or left after cooking.

clue.text: Drink in time involving small amount of liquid? Just the reverse

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one piece holds the other
the roles are swapped: the liquid measure goes round the rest instead

parts.note: ML is a millilitre, a tiny volume
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A drink taken in a moment that holds a little liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' swaps 'involving': the millilitre goes round the rest, not the other way, so 'in' is a letter piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral water, or a fizzy soft drink called a mineral, is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Complaint linked to old arty club

parts.note: a grouch is a grumble

explanation.surface: Grumbling about an old-fashioned arts club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Groucho Club is a London members' club for people in the arts and media.
explanation.definitionFit: The Groucho is a famous Soho private club favoured by artists, writers and media figures.

clue.text: Matches on Saturday will show this game

indicators.note: the word Matches is placed on, that is before, the day's abbreviation
only part of the word Matches is put on show, its tail end, with the opening letters left out

parts.note: taken as written
S is an abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.surface: Saturday's fixtures will feature this game.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter intends a hidden word: 'Matches' followed by the S of Saturday 'will show' the game inside, with 'on' meaning 'followed by'. MAT is the part left unshown.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game, so the game in the clue refers to it.

clue.text: Revolutionary attack knocking out one African town

indicators.note: the letter for one is knocked out, taken away
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to assail is to attack
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A revolutionary attack that knocked out one African town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses ASSAIL to LIASSA, and 'knocking out' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa is a town in north-east Nigeria, which gave its name to Lassa fever.

clue.text: Time in playing tennis is demanding

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the rearranged letters
playing about with letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: A time-in in a tennis match is demanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges TENNIS IS to INSISENT, and T goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent means demanding persistently, refusing to take no for an answer.

clue.text: Temperature rating cut by half around large decorations

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the letter for large
half of the word is cut off, leaving its first half

parts.note: an assessment is a rating or evaluation

explanation.surface: A temperature rating halved around a large figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by half' cuts ASSESSMENT to ASSES, which goes 'around' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassels are hanging tufts of threads used as ornaments on cushions and curtains.

clue.text: Article is recalled about French bits of land in part of Central Europe

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes round the French word
recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
îles is French for islands

explanation.surface: A story recalled about pieces of French territory in Central Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives SIA and 'about' wraps it round the French word for islands, which needs its accent dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region now mostly in Poland, lying in Central Europe.
